# img snapshot

Repository: https://github.com/joshuarli/img
Base: 3213d3c81481fb0f3873f0f4c20e952ea108df91
Branch: master (pushed 2026-11-25, 2026-11-26 twice, and 2026-11-27 for the WebP decoder; the PNG commits are cd28108 and its two parents, rebased onto master 137ad9e, the JPEG decoder is 7c3034e with its standards follow-up f2cf102, the JPEG encoder is c9ec6ab with its standards follow-up 6867940, and the WebP decode facade is d534b6f; the GIF commits start at 8878365 and end at 6df34a9, pushed 2026-11-27).
Commit: 686794007482c8fbecd413c9f8492c2b591d0a08 for `codecs/png` and `codecs/jpeg`; d534b6fc4fe74dea1d9b9e88d7a33cea2146f8f8 for `codecs/webp` and `codecs/webpkit`; 6df34a926dfff462b8b6bfa6524841515ee96796 for `codecs/gif`. The snapshot crates are byte-identical to those directories at their respective commits.
Patch: six local commits on the base. The first makes the native codecs (jpegli, libjpeg-turbo, dav1d, libavif) optional behind a default-on `native-codecs` feature and adds `codecs/png`, the streaming PNG codec exported as `img::png_stream`. The second adds `png_stream::chromium`, a port of Chromium's rust_png_ffi reader and writer: the same png crate options and transformations, `next_interlaced_row`, `next_frame_info`, the Adam7 expand and splat helpers, and the Level1WithUpFilter, Fastest, Fast, Balanced and High encoder levels. The third allows missing documentation on the module. The fourth adds `codecs/jpeg`, the pure-Rust libjpeg-turbo-exact streaming decoder exported as `img::jpeg_stream`, with Chromium's header, orientation, density and ICC metadata behavior and a suspending source. The fifth adds `codecs/jpeg`'s baseline encoder, exported as `img_jpeg::encode_stream` with `EncodeColorSpace`, `Downsample`, `EncodeOptions` and `EncodeError`: the libjpeg-turbo 3.1.0 YCbCr tables, h2v1/h2v2 downsampling, islow integer FDCT, reciprocal quantization, optimal Huffman tables and entropy writer, all as reusable mechanisms; the Chromium canvas policy (quality to downsampling, blend-on-black and the sRGB ICC segment) stays in `crates/jpeg-encode`. The sixth adds `codecs/webp`, the pure-Rust `img_webp` browser-facing WebP decode facade: header features from webpkit's probe, a still or an animation's first composited frame decoded to straight RGBA, and libwebp's fixed-point premultiplied BGRA output (`(channel * alpha * 32897) >> 23`). The VP8/VP8L bitstream mechanisms come from the existing `codecs/webpkit` snapshot (P4suta/webpkit cc1311e, MIT OR Apache-2.0); Chromium's seam and call protocol stay in `crates/webp`.

Ten further commits add `codecs/gif`, a pure-Rust Wuffs-compatible GIF stream decoder exported as `img_gif`: 8878365 introduces the decoder; 5a1b547 keeps a zero loop count infinite; 6c6c600 ignores local build artifacts; d18ab64 matches Wuffs' LZW code space and frame config; 596259e follows Wuffs' deferred LZW code width; fc0ae54 tracks the Wuffs save code for code-width growth and the KwKwK case; 8ec7157 aligns the save code with Wuffs v0.3; c6a9f77 expands the canvas to the first frame bounds; f708489 paints LZW output before reporting bad codes; 490a577 matches Wuffs frame bounds and canvas edge cases (zero-area frames, raw row width for clipped frames, invalid literal widths and empty canvases); 26f5bb8 measures required pixels against the raw frame extent so truncated frames stay partial; and 8bdf3d7 corrects the test expectation for a clipped zero-width frame; 6df34a9 adds canonical `# Errors` sections to the fallible decoder methods. Frame dependency, required-frame, repetition and N32 policy stay in `crates/gif`.

The snapshot contains the `img-png`, `img-jpeg`, `img-webp`, `img-gif` and `webpkit` package sources (`codecs/png`, `codecs/jpeg`, `codecs/webp`, `codecs/gif` and `codecs/webpkit`) and the img licenses. Every package is pure Rust: `img-png` depends on the pinned png crate 0.18.1 used by Chromium, `img-jpeg` and `img-gif` have no external dependency, `img-webp` depends only on the local `webpkit`, and `webpkit` has no required dependency, so none has a `-sys` or C dependency.
